title: Why some countries drive on the left
examples: Why does the UK drive on the left?
Which countries drive on the left?
Has a country ever switched sides of the road?

explain.say: If you travel from India to China, something surprising happens on the roads: cars swap sides! Look at the two groups on the board. In the UK, India, Japan, Indonesia and Kenya, cars drive on the left. In the USA, Brazil, China, Egypt and Mexico, they drive on the right.

draw.text: Why some countries drive on the left

explain.say: Most countries drive on the right, but about a third of all the people in the world live where cars drive on the left. Can you find your country's group? Which side do cars drive on where you live?

So why the difference? Look at the timeline. Long ago, many riders kept to the left. One popular idea: most people are right-handed, so keeping left put their sword arm towards anyone coming the other way, and made it easy to climb onto a horse from the roadside.

Britain's empire spread left-hand driving to places like India, Kenya and Australia. Why must a whole country choose one side?

faq.q: Why do some countries drive on the left?
faq.a: One popular idea is that riders kept left so their right, sword-holding arm faced oncoming people. Britain kept this habit and spread it to many places in its empire.
asks: Why does the UK drive on the left?

faq.q: Why do most countries drive on the right?
faq.a: In France and the USA, wagon drivers kept right, and Napoleon's conquests helped spread right-hand driving across Europe. Many other countries followed.
asks: Why does America drive on the right?

faq.a: Sweden switched from left to right in 1967 and Iceland in 1968, while Samoa switched from right to left in 2009.
asks: Has a country ever switched sides of the road?

faq.q: How many people live where cars drive on the left?
faq.a: About a third of the world's people, in countries such as India, Indonesia, Japan, Pakistan, the UK, Kenya, South Africa and Australia.
asks: Which countries drive on the left?

faq.q: Why does Japan drive on the left?
faq.a: Japan was never a British colony. Historians link it to old customs of keeping left, and to early railways built with British help in the 1800s.

facts: Sweden switched from driving on the left to the right on 3 September 1967, a day known as Dagen H.
Samoa switched from driving on the right to the left in 2009.
